1Summary

The x-ray electron-density channel that conditions VoxBind's density model is cropped in the wrong coordinate frame. The map is downloaded correctly and interpolated correctly — but the 16 Å crop box is placed using CrossDocked2020 receptor coordinates, while the electron-density map lives in the deposited crystallographic frame. The two frames differ, often by a crystal symmetry operation, so the density a structure is conditioned on does not match its pocket.

Pipeline checkVerdictEvidence
Download by protein type (PDBe EDS, PDB-ID parsing, map content) Correct 14gs.ccp4 cell matches deposited 14GS; deposited atoms sit at +1.63σ, 92% on density
Crop & align to CrossDocked2020 Broken Crops in the CrossDocked reference frame, not the map's deposited frame
Interpolation to 64³ @ 0.25 Å Correct Recomputed crop matches the on-disk .npy at corr = 1.000000 — but applied to the wrong region
Bottom line

~64% of density crops are decorrelated from the receptor/ligand the model sees. The 260518 10k density A/B (density vs. noise vs. baseline) is confounded and cannot, as-is, reveal whether density conditioning helps.

2The pipeline & the bug

The density pipeline has three stages:

StageCodeStatus
(i) Download 2Fo-Fc maps from PDBe EDS dataset/00a_data_density_download.pyOK
(ii) Crop a 16 Å box at the ligand centroid crossdocked_xray.py::_crop_densitywrong frame
(iii) Trilinear-interpolate to 64³ @ 0.25 Å crossdocked_xray.py::_crop_densityOK (math)

Root cause

CrossDocked2020 groups structures by binding pocket and superposes every receptor of a pocket onto a shared reference structure. That reference frame generally differs from each structure's own crystallographic frame — frequently by a crystal symmetry operation. The PDBe-EDS map, however, is tied to the deposited crystal frame. _crop_density samples the map at CrossDocked-frame coordinates, so it reads the wrong region of the map.

For the worked example below (14GS, test index 3), a residue-matched Kabsch fit shows the CrossDocked receptor and the deposited structure — the same 255 atoms — are related by a 179.3° rotation + 40.1 Å translation (a C2 crystallographic two-fold), 20.1 Å apart in raw coordinates.

3Evidence — one example, end to end (14GS)

One CrossDocked2020 sample traced through all three stages, each shown for the pipeline (as-is) crop and a frame-corrected crop.

4How the bug was found

The bug is invisible from the source: _crop_density is mathematically correct interpolation. It surfaced only when the data was checked against physical ground truth.

  1. Self-consistency check — a trap. Recomputing the 14gs crop reproduced the on-disk .npy exactly (corr 1.000000). This proves the pipeline is consistent with itself — but a systematic bug is self-consistent too. Stopping here yields a false "all good".
  2. Atoms must sit on density. CRITICAL A 2Fo-Fc map is electron density; protein atoms are where the electrons are. Sampling the map at the receptor pocket-atom coordinates gave +0.06σ, versus −0.05σ for random points — the receptor atoms were indistinguishable from noise. This check is grounded in what the data means, not in what the code does.
  3. Localising it. Was the map misread, or the coordinates wrong? Sampling the map at the deposited 14GS coordinates gave +1.63σ, 92% of atoms on density — the map and the gemmi reading are correct; the CrossDocked coordinates are in the wrong frame.
  4. Root cause & proof. Residue-matched Kabsch quantified the frame error (179° + 40 Å); sampling at the corrected coordinates recovered +1.21σ, proving the bug is both real and fixable.

5Impact on the 10k density A/B

The 260518_voxbind_10k_density arm was trained — and is currently being sampled — on density crops that are correctly aligned only ~1/3 of the time. The zero-initialised density_proj lets the model gracefully ignore an uninformative channel, so density ≈ noise ≈ baseline is the expected outcome regardless of whether density conditioning actually helps. Any A/B result on the current crops should be read as inconclusive, not as evidence against density conditioning.

6The fix

Approach — per-structure frame correction

For every structure, recover the rigid transform CrossDocked-frame → deposited-frame by residue-matched Kabsch against the deposited PDB, then crop the map along the transformed grid. Verified to restore receptor density from +0.06σ to +1.21σ.

  1. Download. Re-fetch the PDBe-EDS .ccp4 maps and the deposited .pdb coordinate files for all 14,735 unique PDB IDs.
  2. Recover transforms. Match each receptor's pocket10 atoms to the deposited structure by (residue number, atom name); Kabsch → rotation, translation, residual RMSD, match count per sample.
  3. Re-crop. Regenerate every crop with _crop_density sampling along the frame-corrected grid → a new xray_crops_aligned/ (the current crops are kept intact).
  4. Drop bad matches. Structures with no deposited PDB, too few matched atoms, or high residual RMSD are marked unavailable; the model falls back to zero density for those.
  5. Retrain. Re-run the density arm on the corrected crops and repeat the A/B.
